turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good afternoon, Thomas, just to confirm full name and date of birth.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thomas Nowak, November 30th, 1985.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Perfect, it's been about three months since we started the acetalopram. How are things?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Better, I'd say.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Maybe halfway better.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'm not lying awake every night anymore, but the worrying is still there most days. What does the worrying look like these days? mostly work. I'm a loan officer at Lakeshore Credit Union and there's a reorganization going on, and my wife Kaja is due in November, so, you know, there's a lot on my mind. My shoulders are tight all the time and I snap at people more than I want to.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Congratulations on the baby, and how's falling asleep?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Still takes me maybe 45 minutes most nights. My brain just won't shut off. You were having panic attacks back in the spring,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: any since we last met?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, none since April. That part's actually gone.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That's great, remind me what dose of acetaloprem you're on. The five milligrams?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Oh no, wait, sorry. I went up to ten after the first two weeks like you said, so ten every morning.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: OK, ten milligrams. Any side effects,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: nausea, sexual side effects, anything like that? No, nothing really. Stomach was a bit off the first week, then fine.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: And the hydroxazine. The 25 milligrams for bad moments. How often are you using it?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Maybe twice in the last month. It works, but it knocks me out.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Anything else you're taking, over -the -counter or supplements?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Magnesium glycinate. 200 milligrams at night. A friend recommended it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That's fine to keep. How much coffee are you drinking? Ah, honestly,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: four cups a day.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Maybe five on bad days. That might be feeding the jitters a bit, any alcohol. A beer on the weekend,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: that's it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I have to ask this every time. Any thoughts of suicide or of harming yourself? No, none. Good, so your GAD7 today is 12. When you started it was 16, so it's moving in the right direction, but it's still in the moderate range. Your blood pressure is 128 over 82 and your pulse is 84. You look a little tense but you're talkative, your mood is anxious, your thinking is clear. Yeah,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: tense is a good word for it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: So I think this is generalised anxiety disorder that's partly responding. You're tolerating the acetalopram well, so I'd like to increase it to 20mg once a day.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Take two of your tense until the new prescription is filled. Okay, that's easy.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Keep the hydroxazine for the rough moments up to once a day and don't drive after you take it. Keep the magnesium. And I'd like you to cut the coffee to two cups a day, nothing afternoon.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That one's going to hurt,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: but okay. Are you still seeing the therapist for CBT? Every other week, yes. Good, keep that going. And as always, if you ever have thoughts of hurting yourself, call or text 988 right away.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'd like to see you back in six weeks, so that's around November 4th before the baby comes. Sounds good. Can you send the summary to my portal? My email changed. It's tamas .noac .fasmil .com.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'll update it, take care, and good luck with the reorganisation.
